papers.title: Charge-conserving creation and annihilation of topological phase singularities in atomically thin semiconductors
papers.abs: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. Our results provide a general strategy for exploring and manipulating topological optical states.

papers.title: Steering of topological criticality in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain via non-Hermitian substitutional impurities
papers.abs: We investigate the topological phase in a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain in the presence of a finite concentration of non-Hermitian substitutional impurities. Our primary focus is the discovery of a deterministic mechanism to actively reconfigure the topological phase boundaries by introducing site-dependent, non-reciprocal intracell and intercell hopping amplitudes. Specifically, breaking the internal structural symmetry of the non-reciprocal impurity hoppings induces a targeted macroscopic displacement of the critical point. This mechanism allows for the controlled expansion or compression of the topological phase strictly via local defect asymmetry. We validate this boundary displacement through finite-size scaling analysis. The extracted correlation length critical exponents ($ν\approx 1.455$ and $ν\approx 1.397$ for symmetric and asymmetric configurations, respectively) confirm a disorder-induced departure from the pristine SSH universality class, with the exponent diverging at high defect densities. We also report an impurity-induced real-to-complex spectral transition geometrically characterized by the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect. Ultimately, our results establish how isolated non-Hermitian asymmetries cooperatively interact to deterministically shift macroscopic topological protection.

Controlling Optical Quantum Interference with Plasmonic Metasurfaces
papers.abs: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. Here, we tackle this problem by presenting a composite quantum plasmonic metasurface operating as an ultrathin non-unitary beamsplitter capable of achieving both single photon bosonic bunching and fermionic anti-bunching interference just by varying the incident photons frequency or changing the design dimensions. The presented metasurface combines a plasmonic grating corrugated by periodic nanoslits that can achieve extraordinary optical transmission with additional nanostripes on top forming nanocavities characterized by localized gap plasmon resonances. The photon-photon interactions are analyzed based on calculating the quantum coalescence metric which accurately portrays the obtained bunching or anti-bunching quantum interference. The presented quantum interference operation is applicable to both fundamental non-classical light interactions and in the design of more applied quantum optical logic gates used in quantum computing and communications.

papers.title: Stacking-Induced Tuning of a Flat-Band Surface State in NbIrTe4
papers.abs: Ternary layered transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) offer high tunability and access to correlated and topological states. However, like the broader family of layered TMDCs, their properties are sensitive to stacking order and interlayer coupling. Here, we investigate the electronic structure and surface states of NbIrTe$_4$, a candidate Weyl semimetal in bulk, and predicted to be a quantum spin Hall insulator in monolayer form. Using scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM), angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), and density-functional theory (DFT), we attribute the strong resonance in tunnelling spectroscopy located approximately 8 meV below the Fermi level to a surface-derived flat band which shows sensitivity to the local stacking order at the surface. In regions where the top layer is laterally shifted, tunnelling spectroscopy instead shows a gap-like feature with intensity near the Fermi level shifted in energy. Combining DFT and quasiparticle interference (QPI) measurements, we find this dramatic change in the spectroscopy in the vicinity of the quasi-1D flat-band surface state becomes dispersive due to a change in the spatial distribution of the density of states in the top two layers. These findings establish NbIrTe$_4$ as a platform where surface band dispersion can be effectively tuned through local structural manipulation.

papers.title: Single-Mode Laser Arrays with Size-Invariant Loss Discrimination
papers.abs: In conventional coupled oscillator lattices and laser arrays, expanding the active volume inevitably causes spectral crowding and degrades spatial uniformity, posing a long-standing barrier to high-power single-mode operation. We uncover a dissipative selection mechanism in sparse star networks that decouples modal selectivity from lattice size constraints. By engineering dissipative auxiliary couplings between a central hub and N peripheral resonators, the system establishes an exact star-Laplacian symmetry. This enforces a target eigenstate that is immune to all lossy channels while maintaining equal amplitude across all main nodes. All competing eigenstates break this symmetry, driving the auxiliary loss and opening a persistent, size-independent modal loss gap that prevents multi-mode competition. Realistic microring simulations validate the robustness of this dark-state isolation under electromagnetic dispersion and mechanism extension to arbitrary arrays is allowed when meets the system's exceptional point. By exploiting graph topology to bypass multi-mode competition, this work establishes a general route toward scalable high-power single-supermode laser arrays and robust state selection in coupled non-Hermitian systems.

Non-local Stabilization and Synchronization of Larmor Precession in Trapped Polariton Condensate Dimer
papers.abs: We demonstrate mutual synchronization of Larmor precessions between spatially separated, optically trapped polariton condensates. We identify the cross-condensate correlation g(2)1,2(τ) as a sensitive metric for condensate coupling. Synchronization of precessions in a condensate dimer is mediated by polariton outflow and resonantly depends on spectral overlap and precession winding. All-optical stirring of one site non-locally increases the pseudo-spin dephasing time of its static neighbor, prolonging phase-locking in a dimer by an order of magnitude. Our work establishes a scalable platform for studying non-equilibrium time-periodically driven systems and for high-speed spinoptronic networks.

papers.title: Observation and control of polariton noise in a thermal Rydberg atom electrometer
papers.abs: The establishment of metrics and control of fundamental noise sources in quantum sensing is a long-standing goal in quantum science and technology. We report on the observation of polariton-mediated optical noise in a thermal Rydberg atom vapor and demonstrate its active control and suppression using a radio-frequency field in Rydberg electrometry. The noise exhibits structured amplification and reduction across the Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency resonance. This reveals a nonlinear slow-light feedback mechanism in which the polariton medium stores and releases probe-field energy. We show that the reference radio-frequency field used in Rydberg heterodyne receivers can also tune the medium into an operating regime where high electromagnetic-field responsivity coincides with reduced optical noise. This operating-point control enables optimization of the electric-field sensitivity within the constraints imposed by Rydberg-polariton physics. These results establish polariton noise as a previously unrecognized intrinsic noise source in thermal Rydberg vapors and the corresponding control method as a crucial aspect of continued efforts to achieve fundamental sensitivity limits in Rydberg electrometry.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal spherical Gaussian pulses
papers.abs: We describe a class of electromagnetic Gaussian modes with spherical spatiotemporal structure that remains invariant during propagation through anomalously dispersive media. The angular profile of the modes is given by spherical harmonics, whose quantization axis can be freely chosen. As a result, the modes support spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum (OAM) configurations with longitudinal and transverse components set by the orientation of the quantization axis. Superpositions of these modes generalize the familiar solution of a chirped pulse that simultaneously focuses and compresses to arbitrary angular structure. The modes are derived through a series of unitary transformations that map the dispersive paraxial wave equation onto a Schrödinger equation with a 3D isotropic harmonic potential. These transformations facilitate the identification of conserved operators for mixed longitudinal and transverse OAM.

papers.title: Optical vortex bullets with large angular momenta
papers.abs: We investigate three-dimensional spatiotemporal optical vortex solitons (light bullets with a toroidal shape) carrying higher-order orbital angular momentum in Kerr media with anomalous group-velocity dispersion and a transversely localized Gaussian profile of the linear refractive index. Stationary vortex bullets with topological charges (winding numbers) $1\leq \ell \leq 4$ are obtained as numerical solutions of the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and their existence, structure and stability are systematically analyzed. In terms of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates, these solutions represent matter-wave solitons with embedded vorticity. We examine the dependence of the solution families on the propagation constant, the depth and width of the guiding profile, and $\ell $. It is found that the increase of $\ell $ requires one to use a stronger or wider waveguiding potential to sustain localized states satisfying the Vakhitov-Kolokolov (VK) stability criterion. VK-complying and non-complying branches of vortex-soliton families are separated by a degenerate Townes branch. Direct simulations reveal that, although the guiding profile substantially suppresses the collapse and extends the propagation distance of vortex bullets, their robustness is ultimately limited by azimuthal instabilities, whose growth is enhanced for values of $\ell $. papers.title: Bicircular light tunable topological phases and nonlinear Hall responses in odd-parity magnets
papers.abs: Altermagnets are an emerging class of magnetic materials that exhibit characteristic features of both ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Odd-wave magnets, where the momentum-dependent spin splitting follows an odd-parity form factor, provide a distinct platform for exploring unconventional magnetic and topological phenomena. In this work, we demonstrate light-induced topological phase transitions in odd-parity magnets driven by bicircular light. We show that a cascade of topological phase transitions occur as the relative amplitude ratio of the two beams is varied. These are accompanied by sharp changes of the quantum metric. We demonstrate that bicircular light unlocks nonlinear Hall responses arising from Berry curvature and quantum metric in irradiated odd-wave magnets, and formulate the underlying selection rules. Our results show that both the topology and the nonlinear responses in odd-parity magnets can be directly controlled by a bicircular drive.

All-Dielectric Tight-Binding Photonics via a Band-Gap Vacuum
papers.abs: Tight-binding photonics bridges condensed-matter physics and optics, providing a powerful framework for engineering band structures and topological phases with light. For photons, however, the vacuum is gapless, so resonators in air carry radiative tails that produce spurious long-range couplings. Here we embed resonators in a photonic band-gap vacuum (BgV), a photonic crystal whose band gap plays for photons the role vacuum plays for bound electrons. The BgV localizes each resonance exponentially, so designed short-range couplings define the lattice Hamiltonian. We thereby experimentally realize a faithful Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes Hamiltonian in an all-dielectric photonic crystal, resolving corner resonances and their orbitals in microwave measurements. Unlike the vacuum surrounding electrons, the BgV is itself designable, controlling relative couplings and closed-loop interference through its band dispersion and Bloch modes. Full-wave calculations and extracted models show that uniformly modifying the BgV, with all resonators fixed, switches the quantized polarization of a two-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger lattice and converts a zero-flux lattice into a $π$-flux one. We also numerically realize three-dimensional pyrochlore and hyperhoneycomb lattices with space groups $R\bar{3}m$ and $C2/c$, the latter a nodal-loop semimetal with topological drumhead surface states. These results establish the BgV as a designable vacuum for all-dielectric tight-binding photonics in two and three dimensions.

papers.title: Engineering topological phenomena via field-driven Weyl motion
papers.abs: We illustrate the field-driven anomalous Hall engineering via the momentum-space motion of Weyl nodes using pyrochlore iridates under a [111] magnetic field as an example. We model the system with a well-established microscopic Hamiltonian and the field effect with the spin rotation from the all-in-all-out to the ferromagnetic state. Tracking the position of Weyl nodes during the spin rotation, we demonstrate macroscopic anomalous Hall conductivity variations are fundamentally driven by Weyl node motions by comparing the full multi-band Kubo formula with the geometric Weyl node separation. The discrepancy occurs only near a critical spin rotation angle, where several Weyl nodes come into close proximity. We reveal that the evolution of anomalous Hall conductivity under the magnetic field agrees with reported experiments in an order-of-magnitude and non-monotonicity. These results elucidate the field-driven dynamics of momentum-space monopoles and provide a framework for understanding transport in strongly correlated topological materials.

papers.title: Activating Nonstandard Axion Electrodynamics in Topological Insulator Materials
papers.abs: The conventional axion response of topological insulators (TIs) is characterized by an isotropic pseudoscalar magnetoelectric (ME) coupling rooted in band topology: the condensed matter analog of the axion field. However, as we reveal here, this and other more general ME responses can arise in existing TI materials from symmetry breaking without requiring nontrivial topology. Indeed, we show that breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries using combined electric and magnetic fields unlocks nonstandard axion electrodynamics via the controllable activation of various tensorial ME couplings, thus, going beyond the standard axion picture. Using a well-established first-principles-informed effective model for Bi-and Sb-based TI materials, we estimate the resulting ME coefficients and make concrete predictions for experiments. In particular, we identify nonreciprocal directional dichroism as a distinctive magneto-optical signature of these ME effects, therefore opening a route to engineer and probe symmetry-induced ME phenomena beyond the conventional topological response.

papers.title: Gerchberg-Saxton Optimized Silicon Metasurface for Sinusoidal Structured-Light Three-Dimensional Imaging
papers.abs: Three-dimensional (3D) optical imaging based on structured illumination has attracted considerable attention in applications including machine vision, robotics, and computational sensing. However, conventional structured-light systems generally rely on bulky projection components, such as digital micromirror devices and diffractive optical elements, which limit system miniaturization and integration. Here, we demonstrate a compact structured-light 3D imaging platform enabled by a silicon dielectric metasurface operating at a near-infrared wavelength of 940 nm. The desired sinusoidal fringe illumination is encoded into the metasurface through a Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) phase optimization algorithm, which converts the target far-field distribution into a nanoscale phase profile and subsequently into silicon nanopillar geometries. The fabricated metasurface generates high-quality sinusoidal structured illumination, which is integrated with a four-step phase-shifting reconstruction method to recover 3D object profiles. The proposed approach provides a compact and scalable solution for miniaturized structured-light projection and optical 3D sensing.

papers.title: Unconventional spin momentum locking and topological domains in twisted slabs of topological insulator Bi$_2$Te$_3$
papers.abs: The three-dimensional topological insulator Bi$_2$Te$_3$ hosts topological Dirac states on its two-dimensional surfaces. These Dirac states show spin-momentum locking, which usually implies a tangential Rashba-like spin texture. One can alter the properties of the Dirac states by dividing a slab of such a material into two thinner halves, modifying the interface by twisting, shifting, and changing the interlayer distance. Using first-principles calculations, we investigate such modified slabs of Bi$_2$Te$_3$. The twisting degree of freedom deserves special attention. To this end, we follow two approaches. On the one hand, we probe different stacking configurations in order to extract parameters relevant for small twist angle Moiré structures. We find non-trivial topology only for some stackings, leading to topological domains on the Moiré scale. On the other hand, we calculate the properties of commensurate twisted supercells. The latter reveals not only flat bands, which are tunable by external pressure, but also radial spin textures with unconventional spin-momentum locking.

papers.title: Topological Splitting of Sondheimer Oscillations in Thin-Film Weyl Semimetals
papers.abs: We discuss topological effects on Sondheimer oscillations in the magnetoresistance of thin-film Weyl semimetals. The Sondheimer oscillations are periodic in magnetic field and originate from the commensurability between the film thickness and the cyclotron-orbit pitch. Using Boltzmann transport theory, we investigate the effects of Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment on the oscillations. We find that the Sondheimer oscillations split into two branches with different frequencies and that each branch becomes chirped because its frequency depends on magnetic field. These features originate from the orbital-Zeeman-induced deformation of the Fermi surface. The same mechanism also applies to Dirac semimetals.

papers.title: Vortexable Chern Bands Sit Exactly on the Topological Floor of Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness
papers.abs: Vortexable Chern bands host ideal fractional Chern insulators. Paired with time-reversed partners by orbital-diagonal on-site attraction, they are the least stiff flat-band superconductors at fixed Chern number $C$, filling, and pairing amplitude. For uniform pairing and a nondegenerate paired state, the exact $T=0$ stiffness determinant is the topological floor times $1+(\Torb/2π|C|)^2\le1+(\TLVP/2π|C|)^2$, where $\Torb$ and $\TLVP$ measure departures from vortexability. Enhancement costs vortexability, and the inequality is strict only if internal components share a site, as in heterostrained bilayers.

papers.title: Boosting fluorescence and polarization with nanophotonics for single-molecule chiral sensing
papers.abs: Detecting chirality is essential in chemistry and biomedicine. Circular dichroism identifies chiral molecules through their differential absorption of circularly polarized light. However, its sensitivity is limited by vanishing absorption at low concentrations. Fluorescence-based methods have already enabled other optical techniques to reach the single-molecule limit and could, in principle, also extend chiral detection to reach this sensitivity regime. They are marred, however, by the combination of weak fluorescence signals and low polarization contrast. To overcome these limitations, we leverage high-index dielectric nanophotonics to simultaneously enhance both fluorescence and polarization for chiral sensing. We propose a reciprocity-based analytical framework for a chiral dipolar emitter coupled to a nanoantenna and reveal the different contributions and trade-offs governing the enhancement of circularly polarized fluorescence. Guided by this insight, we tailor achiral dielectric nanostructures to reach a 1000-fold enhancement of fluorescence intensity together with a 10-fold increase in polarization. Crucially, we show that accounting for extrinsic polarization effects in the angular emission patterns of nanophotonic structures is indispensable for reliable enantiomer discrimination. Our approach opens a realistic path for single-molecule chiral sensing.

papers.title: Realization of valley-controlled orbital angular momentum via inter-orbital coupling
papers.abs: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) represents a fundamental degree of freedom (DoF) for understanding novel phenomena in solids and synthetic lattices. However, the generation and control of OAM in lattice systems remain challenging. Here, we experimentally observe valley-controlled OAM states in inversion-symmetry-broken photonic honeycomb lattices consisting of s- and higher-orbital sublattices. These OAM states manifest as chiral vortex arrays in real space. By selectively exciting s-orbital modes carrying no initial OAM at either the K or K' valley, we observe higher-orbital OAM modes generated via inter-orbital coupling in neighboring sites. Specifically, s-p orbital coupling generates OAM states with topological charge l=+1 or l=-1, while s-d orbital coupling yields higher-charge OAM states with l=+2 or l=-2. The sign of the topological charge is determined by the valley DoF, enabling deterministic control of vortex chirality across the entire array. Our theory further reveals that a local vortex-chirality symmetry enforces the valley-dependent selection of vortex chirality at the K and K' valleys, establishing a direct connection between the valley DoF and real-space vortex chirality. These results establish a versatile platform for engineering chiral vortex arrays via orbital physics and exploring orbital- and topology-mediated phenomena in photonic systems and beyond.

papers.title: Charge-Selective Displacement of Spatiotemporal Optical Vortices at a Spatially Uniform Time Boundary
papers.abs: At a spatially uniform, in-plane-isotropic time boundary, the transverse displacement of a spatiotemporal optical vortex changes sign with its topological charge, despite a charge-independent conversion weight. Radial spectral filtering couples to the vortex phase while preserving identical converted spectral intensities for opposite charges. For a narrow scalar Gaussian spectrum, the displacement follows the logarithmic slope of the spectral weight and occurs with zero mean transverse momentum. In a finite pumped GaAs waveguide, unequal attenuation during extraction adds angular deflection. Independent Maxwell--Drude simulations test this extraction-induced response and give $\pm42$~mrad before detector filtering. Calculated centroid traces at multiple planes separate propagation-induced drift from position offsets.

Turning Number and the Geometry of Disorder-Induced Topology
papers.abs: The geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps derived from the zero-frequency single-particle Green's function provides a route to a refined topological characterization of quantum systems beyond the noninteracting clean limit. The central idea is to complement standard topological invariants by invariants that characterize the geometry of the map itself. As a paradigmatic example, we study the one-dimensional chiral Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with disorder, where the topological Hamiltonian defines a planar Bloch loop. In addition to its conventional winding number, this loop possesses an integer turning number that characterizes the winding of its tangent vector. We identify turning-number transitions that occur while the topological Hamiltonian remains finite and spectrally gapped, driven solely by a vanishing tangent vector of the Bloch loop, and obtain an extended phase diagram with additional topological structure beyond the winding-number classification. Asymptotic analysis predicts the emergence and disorder dependence of the corresponding transition regime, in agreement with the numerical results. Our findings establish the geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps as an additional source of topological structure beyond conventional classifications.

papers.title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
papers.abs: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moiré materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced en

papers.title: Second Chern Number Protected Gapless Vortex Modes in Superconducting Weyl Semimetals
papers.abs: We have studied the vortex bound states of superconducting linear and quadratic Weyl semimetals with time reversal symmetry. For vortex with vorticity $n$ (vortex line along $z$ direction) and Weyl semimetals with Weyl point chirality $χ$, there are $\vert nχ\vert$ gapless vortex modes around the location of each Weyl point in superconducting Weyl semimetals. We show that the appearance of $\vert nχ\vert$ gapless vortex modes originates from the imbalanced pumping of flux bound states between Chern insulators obtained at $k_{z}$ and $-k_{z}$ in Weyl semimetals. Such a physical picture is verified by numerical calculations on lattice models. Moreover, the gapless modes around each Weyl point can be characterized by the second Chern number defined in a synthetic four-dimensional space based on the effective BdG Hamiltonian. Finally, these gapless vortex modes are found to be robust against rotational symmetry-breaking terms.

papers.title: A Chiral Superlattice Route to Spin-Split Topological Antiferromagnetism
papers.abs: The interplay between chirality and magnetism is a profound topic, spanning particle physics, condensed matter, chemistry and origin of life. In this paper, we study this interplay in the new antiferromagnet (AFM) UOTe, and we report a chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological phenomena from collinear antiferromagnetism. Pristine UOTe is a collinear AFM without Berry curvature or spin-split bands. However, we identify the spontaneous formation of a chiral superlattice in UOTe, which can be viewed as frozen chiral phonons at finite wave vector. When electrons move through the chiral superlattice, their orbital Bloch wavefunction and quantum geometry are modulated by the strong chiral superlattice potential, generating large Berry curvature in the chiral superlattice, which we detect by the nonlinear Hall effect. At 150 K, the chiral superlattice induced Berry curvature couples to the collinear AFM order, generating a giant anomalous Hall angle ~0.14 abruptly near $T_N$ that is among the largest in bulk magnets. Moreover, our spin Hanle precession measurement shows that the chiral superlattice also generates spin-polarized current from the collinear AFM, a long-standing goal in spintronics. We shed light on the supermodulation formation mechanism based on chemical ion size and physical interlayer-intralayer energy competitions, using which we propose a design principle to discover similar bond-mismatch superlattices, providing a chiral superlattice pathway through real space engineering of quantum geometry.

papers.title: Boundary Element Modeling for THz-SNOM Near-Field Probes
papers.abs: Terahertz scanning near-field optical microscopy (THz-SNOM) enables spatially and spectrally resolved investigation of low-energy collective and topological states in quantum materials and nano-structured devices by exploiting the strongly localized near field generated by a polarized atomic force microscopy (AFM) tip. Because the THz near-field response is highly sensitive to tip geometry, understanding how geometric parameters control field confinement and decay is essential for selecting tip designs that provide the spatial resolution required for specific experiments. In this work, we develop a boundary element method (BEM) for modeling the electrostatic near-field of a conducting AFM tip in response to an external background field. The tip is represented by a simplified closed, blunt-cone geometry with its surface discretized into panels using increased mesh density near the apex. A modified Green's function is used to calculate interactions between surface panels, while an augmented linear system simultaneously enforces the equipotential boundary condition on the conducting surface and overall charge neutrality to determine the induced surface-charge distribution. We validate the BEM by comparing the resulting near-field decay with that obtained from a three-dimensional quasi-static COMSOL Multiphysics simulation. The BEM accurately reproduces the COMSOL field-decay behavior while requiring orders of magnitude fewer mesh elements and substantially reducing computational cost. papers.title: Orbital Angular Momentum Currents and Textures in a Multiorbital Double Helix
papers.abs: The microscopic origin of chirality induced spin selectivity (CISS) in biomolecular structures has traditionally been discussed in terms of spin orbit coupling and spin angular momentum. However, orbital angular momentum (OAM) is increasingly recognized as a more direct electronic response to molecular chirality. A helical hopping network built only from s orbitals can support an itinerant orbital moment and an orbital Edelstein response, but such a basis has no local atomic OAM and therefore omits the complementary contribution arising from coherence among active p orbitals. Here we construct a six-band multiorbital double helix model parameterized by characteristic B form DNA geometry and hopping scales. The model incorporates major minor groove asymmetry, an axial base pair offset representing stagger, and compositional inequivalence between the two strands, providing structural control parameters with which the orbital response can be tuned. Inter strand hybridization generates a full three component atomic OAM texture in the corotating local helical frame, including a radial component absent in the corresponding single helix model. We separately evaluate the itinerant OAM using the Bloch wave packet formulation of orbital magnetization and identify an additional inter-strand circulation channel unique to the double-helix connectivity. The resulting atomic and itinerant responses have distinct microscopic origins, magnitudes, and temperature dependences, establishing a multiorbital framework for geometry controlled angular momentum generation and transport in chiral mol

papers.title: Symmetry constraints on magnon-induced dynamics of skyrmion helicity in frustrated magnets
papers.abs: The helicity of a magnetic skyrmion in a centrosymmetric frustrated magnet is a soft collective coordinate and a candidate variable for encoding quantum information. Its coherence is ultimately influenced by coupling to the magnon environment, which is commonly incorporated only phenomenologically. Here we combine a microscopic Keldysh treatment of the helicity--magnon coupling to resolve the contribution of individual magnon modes to the effective helicity dynamics. In the U(1)-symmetric model, the magnon bath generates, to leading order, a reactive helicity mass renormalization. When U(1) symmetry is broken, additional direct helicity--magnon couplings become allowed. In the presence of finite magnon lifetimes, these couplings generate an Ohmic contribution to the low-frequency helicity dynamics. The spatial symmetry of the perturbation determines which magnon sectors contribute to this damping, providing mode-resolved selection rules for the helicity--magnon coupling. Thus, we establish a microscopic connection between helicity dynamics and the excitation spectrum of frustrated skyrmions and identify the symmetry constraints governing dissipation of helicity-based quantum states.

Broadband chiroptical sensing with two-mode subwavelength grating waveguides
papers.abs: Engineering local optical chirality in planar photonic structures offers a route to selective and enhanced light-matter interactions with chiral media. Here, we introduce periodic dielectric waveguides that support chiral evanescent fields through the interaction of two nearly degenerate waveguide modes. We develop a perturbation theory for such a waveguide covered by a chiral layer, relating chirality-induced modal coupling and propagation-constant corrections to measurable intermodal power conversion and differential transmission. Whereas modal detuning confines the chiral response of a symmetric waveguide to a narrow spectral range, mode hybridization in an asymmetric waveguide creates individual eigenmodes that carry nonzero local chirality over a broad spectral range. We show that modal dichroism in realistic lossy waveguides can produce a significant background differential transmission signal. Such a background, however, can be suppressed by comparing transmission through two asymmetric waveguides with opposite structural asymmetries, allowing the chiral response to be reliably extracted. Together, these findings provide a basis for developing integrated photonic components with locally chiral fields, including waveguides, metasurfaces, and resonators.

papers.title: Topological edge and domain-wall phonons in the mass-dimerized diatomic chain: complex band structure, Zak phase, and spectral unfolding
papers.abs: The one-dimensional chain with alternating masses is the simplest mechanical system with a topological band structure. We give a fully analytical account of its localized vibrations built on the complex band structure. The evanescent Bloch waves available at each frequency are matched directly to force balance at a free end or a domain wall, without transfer matrices, which yields closed-form frequencies and decay lengths for every localized mode. The free-end mode sits at a branch point of the complex band structure, where the acoustic and optical sheets join and the decay is fastest. For uniform springs, a sharp wall between the two mass orderings hosts one in-gap mode, symmetric at the light$\mid$light wall and antisymmetric at the heavy$\mid$heavy wall, and an adiabatic construction shows that these are the same topological mode; the light$\mid$light wall also binds a non-topological mode above the optical branch. Spectral unfolding makes this classification visible in momentum space: the sign of the Bloch factor sets the zone-center or zone-boundary character of each mode, and its magnitude sets the width. The Zak phase, quantized by inversion, identifies the modes of topological origin and fixes a half-integer mode count per band at a wall, while the chiral symmetry known to be hidden in strain coordinates explains which frequencies are pinned.

Programming the Nonlinear Optics of a Nanoporous Photonic Metamaterial by Confined Crystallization
papers.abs: A membrane traversed by a dense array of nanochannels acts as a photonic metamaterial: with channels far smaller than the wavelength of light, the optical response is set by the architecture rather than by the constituent materials. Here each nanochannel is turned into a nonlinear optical meta-atom by filling anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) with benzil (BZL), a noncentrosymmetric molecular crystal, and the crystallization pathway programs their orientation. In free-standing membranes every channel solidifies independently, the orientations remain uncorrelated, and the effective second-harmonic generation (SHG) response is nearly polarization isotropic; its magnitude follows a core - shell model in which an optically inactive interfacial layer of 2.6 nm reduces the active volume of each meta-atom, reproducing on bare alumina the value previously found on alkyl-grafted silica and indicating a host-insensitive limit. Seeding crystallization from a bulk benzil layer instead aligns the meta-atoms over submillimeter domains and produces a macroscopically anisotropic effective susceptibility. Channel diameters from 32 to 270 nm span the transition out of the subwavelength regime, and the anomalous directional SHG emission reported here is confined to the metamaterial limit. Confined crystallization thus offers a route to nonlinear optical metamaterials whose effective susceptibility tensor is written during processing.

Attraction from repulsion in an interacting Chern band: chiral superconductivity, generalized Hall crystals, and competing fractional Chern insulators
papers.abs: Experiments realizing strong interactions in partially filled Chern bands have observed fractional Chern insulators (FCIs), superconductors, and topological crystals in close proximity. Yet the microscopic relation between them remains poorly understood. Here, we use tensor network simulations to study repulsively interacting spinless fermions in a tunable topological band of the checkerboard lattice. We characterize the competing phases and identify key features of the experimental phenomenology. FCIs from the Jain sequence transition into chiral p-wave superconductivity both below and above half filling as the band dispersion is enhanced. By contrast, at half filling, a generalized Hall crystal with quantized Hall conductance and a doubled unit cell forms for sufficiently strong coupling. Surprisingly, a weak-coupling approach starting from a metallic parent state captures the nature of both ordered phases at intermediate coupling. We find that fluctuations in the metal generate longer-range attraction, which we analyze within the random-phase approximation. This approach captures the pairing symmetry as well as the radial form factors of the Cooper pairs, and incorporating this attraction into Hartree-Fock selects the observed Hall crystal. Together, these results identify fluctuation-induced attraction from repulsion as a common microscopic ingredient of ordering, while our tensor network computations establish the direct competition of both phases with FCIs.

papers.title: Comment on "Skyrmion Hall Effect in Altermagnets"
papers.abs: In their Letter, Jin et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 196701 (2024)] predict a transverse velocity $v_y$ for skyrmions driven by spin-transfer torque (STT), known as skyrmion Hall effect (SkHE), in d-wave altermagnets. Usually, the SkHE emerges from the skyrmion's topological charge which here cancels between sublattices. Instead, Jin et al. attribute the SkHE to the dimensionless quadrupole tensor $A_{ij}$. The result in their Eq. (12) is fitted to micromagnetic simulations, yielding a finite value for $A_{xy}$. However, via the divergence theorem, $A_{ij}$ simplifies to a boundary integral that vanishes for a sufficiently smooth and localized texture. In this Comment, we substantiate our claim from Ref. [2] that the numerically observed SkHE by Jin et al. for a micromagnetic model with standard Zhang-Li STT in the individual sublattices is merely a discretization artefact.

The role of distributed friction dynamics on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and simulations
papers.abs: This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.

papers.title: Frequency comb stability, bistability, and self-starting in normal dispersion microresonators
papers.abs: Recent work has demonstrated that it is possible to generate frequency combs in normal dispersion microresonators by taking advantage of fabricated mode coupling that induces a mode split. In particular, photonic crystal resonators periodically modulate the microresonator's width, which geometrically creates mode coupling. In contrast to frequency combs generated by microresonators in the anomalous dispersion regime, which are typically generated using bright solitons, the frequency combs generated by normal dispersion regime microresonators are dark pulses that are commonly referred to as dark solitons or platicons. In this work, we examine the linear stability of platicons in the pump-detuning and pump-power parameter space as the mode split strength and cavity dispersion is varied. Our work reveals a broad region of stability for platicons. Our work also reveals the existence of fingers at high power at whose boundaries a sharp transition occurs and inside of which platicon solutions are bistable. Finally, we investigate the overlap of the region where platicons are stable with the region where continuous waves are modulationally unstable, and it is possible for a platicon to self-start. Simulations show that platicons consistently self-start inside this region.

papers.title: Exciton superfluidity in two-dimensional bilayers at zero and high magnetic fields
papers.abs: We study interlayer exciton superfluidity versus layer separation in two-dimensional electron-hole bilayers at zero magnetic field and quantum Hall bilayers at total filling $ν_T=1$. Unscreened Hartree-Fock theory predicts coherence at every finite separation, with an energy scale decaying inversely with separation at large distances. We examine how screening, correlations, and spatial instabilities modify this prediction. At zero field, we solve the linearized gap equation with the full momentum and frequency dependence of the interaction screened within the random-phase approximation, without an imposed cutoff. The apparent plasmon enhancement of pairing in the ladder approximation is largely cancelled by the second-order crossed-rung correction. Static screening determines the leading pairing exponent in the controlled high-density limit at fixed separation. At large separation, the pairing scale falls exponentially with squared separation while the instability persists. Extending this result to fixed density assumes Fermi-liquid layers and higher-order dynamical corrections subleading to the static pairing interaction. At high field, we obtain an analytic uniform Hartree-Fock saddle point in the lowest Landau level, coherent at every finite separation. Within Hartree-Fock theory, its finite-wave-vector collective-mode instability favors an excitonic supersolid, distinguishing loss of spatial uniformity from loss of coherence. We conjecture that the quantum Hall bilayer evolves continuously toward weak pairing of composite fermions, with a scale far below the mean-field

papers.title: Large in-plane optical anisotropy in epitaxial CrN(113) films
papers.abs: CrN, a transition-metal nitride crystallizing in the cubic rocksalt structure, exhibits a unique combination of mechanical robustness, semiconducting behavior, and thermoelectric functionality. To date, however, CrN has been synthesized primarily as polycrystalline material or as epitaxial films grown along high-symmetry orientations such as (001) and (111). Here, we prepare epitaxial CrN(113) films on AlN(11\bar{2}2) templates by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. The low-symmetry interface and highly direction dependent lattice mismatch are expected to modify the physical properties of CrN relative to the bulk material. Indeed, variable-angle spectroscopic ellipsometry in the photon-energy range from 1.25 to 5 eV reveals a surprisingly strong polarization dependence of the optical response despite the nearly strain-free cubic crystal structure of the films. The pseudo-optical constants n and k differ by more than 10% for orthogonal in-plane polarizations throughout the investigated spectral range. We evaluate possible origins of this effect and conclude that it most likely arises from anisotropic surface morphology of CrN(113), which creates a metasurface acting as a subwavelength grating in the strongly absorbing regime.

papers.title: Thermal Confinement in Plasmonic Nanoparticles under Generalised Pulsed Illumination
papers.abs: Thermal confinement is a key parameter in photothermal applications, as it determines the spatial extent of the region affected by the generated heat. In this work, we develop a numerical treatment to quantify thermal confinement in spherical plasmonic nanoparticles under excitation conditions ranging from ultrashort pulses to the continuous-wave regime. The model combines generalized optical heating with a finite-difference solution of the transient heat equation and explicitly accounts for finite interfacial thermal conductance. To characterize the spatial distribution of heat, we introduce a thermal confinement radius defined from the temporal temperature envelope in the surrounding medium. We demonstrate that pulse duration acts as a highly effective, tuneable parameter to govern thermal confinement. Notably, we quantitatively show that finite interfacial thermal conductance can induce deviations of up to 20% in the spatial confinement radius and over 60% in the transient thermal construct under ultrashort excitation. By comparing the characteristic dimensions of representative targeting ligands with the resulting thermal-confinement length scales, we show how pulse duration can be precisely tailored to control target heating. These results provide a unified framework for predicting nanoscale heat localization paving the way for the rational design of high precision thermoplasmonic applications.

papers.title: Displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector using quantum tomography of photon orbital angular momentum states
papers.abs: Gravitational waves (GWs) induce quantum transitions between photon orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) states with amplitudes $α_{\pm}$. Exploiting this effect, we present a displacement-noise-free detection framework that extracts GW information from the OAM Hilbert space. Parametrized quantum state tomography of the GW-induced OAM sidebands enables a single V-shaped detector to resolve all seven wave parameters: the frequency, propagation direction, two polarization amplitudes, and initial phase of each polarization. Direct detection of the sidebands yields a weak signal of approximately $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{W}$. We therefore introduce a stronger reference state $r |0>_{\mathrm{P}}$, with $r=0.01$, to enhance the detected signal. For an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $γ=0.1$, an incident light power of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, a wavelength of $λ_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$, and GW amplitudes of $A=10^{-18}$, we estimate sideband transition amplitudes of $|α_{\pm}|\sim10^{-10}$ and signal powers of order $1\,\mathrm{nW}$, scaling as $P_{\mathrm{BS}}α_{\pm}\propto P_{\mathrm{BS}}ANLγ/λ_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The shot-noise-limited sensitivity floor is $S^{1/2}_n=1.6\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$. Because the scheme measures OAM transition amplitudes rather than differential arm lengths, it is intrinsically free from displacement noise and provides a broadband probe of GWs, specifically bridging the $0.1$--$10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.

papers.title: Localized high-Q resonances enable electrically defined beam steering in lithium niobate metasurfaces
papers.abs: High-speed beam steering for LiDAR and optical communication requires independent, reconfigurable control of optical phase. We demonstrate a metasurface combining lithium niobate's Pockels effect with high-Q (Q > 1700) silicon guided-mode resonance nanoantennas whose localized resonances allow individual electro-optic control at a 1 $μ$m pitch. Identical arrays steer light to 53.5$^\circ$ or 32.4$^\circ$, with the angle set by the bias pattern rather than antenna geometry. We measure 18.0% 0th-order modulation depth, 0.09% of incident power in the steered order, and a 940 MHz detected modulation bandwidth. Mode-overlap analysis shows how inter-element coupling limits usable Q, providing design rules for compact, high-speed beam steering.

Orbitronics in Zero-dimensional Graphene Nanoflakes via Electrode Coupling
papers.abs: We show that graphene nanoflakes realize a previously unexplored form of orbitronics in which orbital currents emerge in the absence of intrinsic angular momentum of the constituent atoms. Starting with a hexagonal graphene nanoflake, we demonstrate the presence of energy-degenerate eigenstates with opposite non-zero expectation values of the angular momentum. Placing electrodes in an appropriate configuration on the flake couples the reservoirs more strongly to one of the two opposite-angular-momentum states, yielding a chiral current that carries a net orbital angular momentum. The resulting circulating orbital currents generate magnetic fringe fields that are experimentally accessible with spin centers or superconducting quantum interference magnetometers, providing avenues for their experimental realization. Finally, our work establishes a new platform for exploring and studying orbitronics in zero-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Designing Hamiltonians with Exactly Flat Higher-Vortexable Bands
papers.abs: The zero modes of the Aharonov-Casher Hamiltonian form an exactly flat, vortexable Chern band in any nonuniform magnetic field, analogous to the lowest Landau level. We ask which local Hamiltonians host exactly flat higher-vortexable bands. For a scalar Hamiltonian, an exactly flat first-vortexable band requires a mass proportional to the local field; the Dirac analogue has the same structure. For periodic Bernal bilayer graphene with nonzero mean flux, the exact zero-mode pair is genuinely first-vortexable if and only if the interlayer hopping has nonzero mean; zero-mean hopping instead gives a decomposable pair. Multiorbital models yield exact higher-vortexable chains to arbitrary order, while remaining first order in momentum.

papers.title: Cavity-tunable Pseudospin-Hall Topology and Edge Transport
papers.abs: Topological edge states are a hallmark of topological phases, with their existence tied to bulk band topology through bulk-edge correspondence. In photonic pseudospin-Hall systems, these states exhibit pseudospin-momentum locking, with lattice interactions and interface geometry determining each pseudospin's propagation direction. Reversing the pseudospin-dependent propagation direction without altering the lattice configuration or excitation handedness remains a fundamental challenge in controlling topological edge transport. Here, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate cavity-tunable topological edge transport in a microwave metasurface embedded within a metallic cavity. Varying the cavity height reshapes resonator interactions, driving band inversion and topological phase transition while preserving the lattice geometry. For a fixed domain-wall configuration, this transition reverses the propagation direction associated with each pseudospin while preserving pseudospin-momentum locking. Excitations with the same handedness are observed to launch edge waves propagating in opposite directions at their respective edge-band frequencies determined by the cavity height. These results establish cavity electrodynamics as an external means of controlling the bulk topology and reconfiguring the directional response of topological interfaces, creating new opportunities for topological wave routing in fixed photonic lattice structures.

papers.title: From Single-Particle Thermal Asymmetry to Collective Control: Janus Plasmonic Colloids for Photothermal Applications
papers.abs: Janus nanoheaters provide a route to break the spatial symmetry of thermoplasmonic heating and generate directionally biased thermal gradients at the nanoscale. However, in realistic photothermal scenarios, nanoheaters rarely act as isolated objects, but rather operate within colloidal assemblies where collective thermal and electromagnetic effects reshape the local temperature landscape. Here, we investigate how the intrinsic thermal asymmetry of a single Janus plasmonic nanoheater is transformed when moving from isolated particles to planar random arrays under continuous-wave illumination. Using coupled electromagnetic and steady-state heat-transfer simulations, we first quantify the finite spatial range over which the single-particle Janus signature remains detectable. We show that neighboring nanoheaters introduce two competing effects: a nearly symmetric collective thermal background that screens and homogenizes the Janus factor, and short-range neighbor-induced asymmetries that partially compensate this screening when interparticle distances become comparable to the spatial extent of the single-particle thermal anisotropy. We derive a closed-form analytical model for the array-averaged Janus factor as a function of nanoparticle number and surface density. The model predicts the screening-dominated regime from single-particle quantities and identifies deviations associated with near-field neighbor-induced contributions at higher densities. papers.title: Near-field contributions to cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer
papers.abs: Embedding materials in optical cavities has emerged as a powerful strategy for controlling their physical properties. In this context, increasing attention has been devoted to the thermal Purcell effect, which describes how the radiative heat transfer between a material and its photonic environ- ment can be modified by the electromagnetic boundary conditions imposed by the cavity. Here, we investigate near-field effects in cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer in planar cavities composed of realistic, dissipative gold mirrors, extending previous work that considered ideal mirrors. We iden- tify the conditions under which near-field effects lead to a substantial enhancement of heat transfer between the material and a photonic thermal bath relative to free space, owing to the strong modi- fication of the photonic local density of states by evanescent modes within the cavity. In particular, we find that radiative heat flow can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude in cavities ranging from nanometer to micrometer scales, depending on the absorber frequency and dipole orientation. These findings suggest that near-field effects may be relevant to polariton chemistry experiments and other systems operating within this cavity length-scale regime. Our results add to the idea that cavities can modify material properties not only by engineering vacuum fluctuations in the strong light-matter coupling regime, but also by controlling radiative dissipation and heat transfer.

papers.title: Polaritonic self-hybridized critical coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
papers.abs: Maximizing the absorption of exciton-polaritons in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) under critical coupling conditions is crucial for developing high-efficiency polariton-based photodetectors, solar cells, and perfect absorbers. Here, we propose a polaritonic critical self-hybridized coupling between Brillouin zone folding driven quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBIC) mode and A excitons in a bulk WS2 metasurface. This polaritonic critical coupling shows robust behavior with respect to the asymmetric parameters of the involved BZF-QBIC mode, in contrast to the asymmetry-sensitive conventional QBIC-based critical coupling. By changing the height of WS2 metasurfaces, we observe a typical anti-crossing behavior with a Rabi splitting of 246.5 meV. Moreover, the maximum absorption value of 0.5 for exciton-polaritons is achieved at the polaritonic critical coupling condition. The large population of excitons provided by bulk WS2 is essential for achieving polaritonic critical coupling and can further enhance polaritonic absorption. This work enables the realization of robust, high-absorption self-hybridized polaritonic critical coupling in TMDCs, and further expedite their applications in high-absorption low-dimensional polaritonic devices.

papers.title: Inferring Transition-Dipoles from Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy with Deep Learning
papers.abs: Two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy is a powerful nonlinear technique for probing vibrational couplings, anharmonicities, coherence, and molecular dynamics. Among the microscopic parameters encoded in 2D IR spectra, transition dipoles are fundamental quantities that characterize molecular structure and govern light-matter interactions. However, reconstructing these quantities from spectroscopic data remains a challenging inverse problem. Here, we introduce a physics-informed convolutional neural network (CNN), Spec2DipoleNet, trained on 2D IR spectra generated via the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (NHH) method. This multi-task CNN reconstructs the transition dipole matrices under physically-motivated masking constraints. On the validation set, the model achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.085, an $R^2$ of 0.97, and a normalized cross-correlation of 0.98. It reliably recovers matrix elements associated with allowed transitions, while larger deviations are observed for nominally forbidden transitions. Our results suggest that transition dipole operators can be quantitatively inferred from 2D IR spectra, highlighting the potential of physics-informed deep learning for extracting microscopic quantum parameters from multidimensional spectroscopic data.

papers.title: All-Optical Ultrafast Pure Spin Current in the Altermagnet Cr2SO
Pressure engineering of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moiré superlattices
papers.abs: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. Moreover, we demonstrate efficient pressure control over the interplay between charges and both intralayer and interlayer excitons: the intralayer charge-transfer exciton becomes less sensitive to doping, likely due to reduced charge-transfer character; in contrast, the interlayer exciton exhibits enhanced exciton-charge repulsion. Our results establish hydrostatic pressure as a powerful tuning knob for engineering bosonic quasiparticles and Bose-Fermi interactions in moiré materials.

papers.title: Femtosecond all-optical polarization manipulation of harmonic generation in an anisotropic strongly coupled plasmon-epsilon-near-zero metasurface
papers.abs: Ultrafast manipulation of light polarization plays a key role in modern high-speed photonics and optoelectronic operations. However, most current polarization-active modulation schemes are restricted by a limited operating wavelength range (visible to infrared), narrow-band resonant fundamental wavelength working condition, and relatively long modulation time (> 1 picosecond). Here, by taking advantage of the transient anisotropic nonlinearity of optical strong coupling between the epsilon-near-zero mode of indium tin oxide (ITO) film and polarization-selective plasmonic resonance, we achieve femtosecond polarization manipulation of broadband light that spans ultraviolet (UV) to visible region by controlling harmonic generation of the signal light under resonant pumping. We demonstrate polarization elliptic rotation of 23.3° at 407 nm for third-harmonic generation (THG) and 55.0° at 610 nm for second-harmonic generation (SHG) simultaneously within ~600 fs. In addition, the strongly coupled system can also serve as a universal femtosecond polarization modulation source, imprinting a 32.9° polarization rotation in the UV region by converting the modulation information of the fundamental signal light to that of THG light via a uniform ITO film in a cascaded configuration. Our study establishes a new paradigm for UV-based, ultrahigh-speed broadband polarization photonics with direct implications for high-speed optical information processing and programmable nonlinear photonic devices.

papers.title: A compact six-beam 3D magneto-optical trap based on multifunctional metasurface chips
papers.abs: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs), indispensable to cold-atom-based quantum computing and quantum precision measurement, are increasingly desired in compact and stable form. Particularly, the six-beam 3D-MOT, distinguished by symmetric geometry and superior trapping performance, finds particularly broad applications. Conventional implementations, however, rely on complex and bulky free-space optics, hindering miniaturization, practical assembly, and long-term stability. Here, we demonstrate a compact six-beam 3D-MOT system that employs two multifunctional optical metasurface chips to implement the optical-field functionalities required for cooling and trapping atoms. By combining two metasurface chips and a vacuum cell, a photonic-integrated cell module (PICM) is implemented as the core assembly and the volume is only" 73*73*107 mm^3" . In success, 1.3 * 10^3 Rb atoms are trapped and cooled to the temperature of ~183 μK. It should be noticed that the laser beam is guided to the metasurface through optical fiber, thus such fully fiber-coupled architecture enables straightforward and stable operations. We believe that this work would pave a practical route toward compact and portable 3D-MOT.

papers.title: Strong field confinement in air and enhanced optical Kerr nonlinearity of high-index star-shaped pore membrane metasurfaces
papers.abs: The optical Kerr effect in high-refractive-index membrane metasurfaces patterned with a square lattice of five-pointed star-shaped pores is investigated numerically using gallium phosphide as a model material. The star geometry supports resonances with pronounced electromagnetic energy confinement, including an anapole state. The sharp tips of the star-shaped pores concentrate the electric energy density in air, exceeding that of Mie voids by a factor of seven. The effective second-order refractive index is enhanced by up to three orders of magnitude relative to bulk GaP, with the largest values obtained near the anapole resonances. The nonlinear response remains stable under polarization rotation and random misalignment of the nanoholes, indicating tolerance to fabrication imperfections. These results establish star-shaped pore lattices in freestanding membranes as a promising platform for nonlinear optics exploiting strong field confinement.

papers.title: Chern insulator optics
papers.abs: Chern insulators have optical properties that are strikingly different than ordinary chiral media. Unlike the natural optical activity of the latter, which is a finite-wavelength effect arising from spatial dispersion, the optical activity of a Chern insulator is already present in the long-wavelength limit, and exhibits a striking directional asymmetry in the propagation of circularly polarized light. We study this unnatural optical activity using a recently developed field theory for Chern insulators. For bulk Chern insulators, we derive the normal-incidence transmission and reflection coefficients of multilayer structures, identify the associated Faraday and Kerr angles, and show that these optical rotations provide a direct optical signature of topology at low frequencies. We also show that an interface between bulk Chern insulators can act as a kind of mirror, completely reflecting light at normal incidence when the Chern invariants have opposite signs. Moving to a more realistic model of a two-dimensional current sheet, we study the Faraday and Kerr effects in a thin film of $\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{Bi}_2\mathrm{Te}_4$ in its Chern insulator phase. The predicted rotations are many orders of magnitude larger than those of optically active media of comparable thickness that are topologically trivial.

papers.title: Topologically Protected Surface Acoustic Wave Edge States in Phononic Integrated Circuits
papers.abs: Phononic integrated circuits enable the development of compact systems to manipulate radio frequency signals through interconnected networks of acoustic waveguides. Introducing topologically protected robustness in these circuits to counter fabrication imperfections and local perturbations, remains a challenge. This work presents a validated modeling framework for topologically protected edge states using surface acoustic waves in etch-defined waveguides consisting of scandium aluminum nitride on silicon carbide, directly comparing analytical, full-wave numerical simulation, and laser Doppler vibrometer measured experimental approaches and their agreement. This work represents the first experimental demonstration of topological edge states on a ScAlN on SiC platform, validated through direct quantitative comparison with analytical and numerical analyses, with future implications for topological protection in phononic and optomechanical integrated circuit platforms.

papers.title: Pseudo-relativistic fermions and topological states in zinc-blende semiconductors and their heterostructures (Habilitation thesis)
papers.abs: Tracing my scientific path from many-body physics in semiconductor nanostructures to topological quantum matter, this Habilitation à diriger des recherches (HDR) memoir presents only part of my research since defending two PhD theses in Toulouse and Nizhny Novgorod in 2011. Focusing on pseudo-relativistic fermions and topological states in zinc-blende semiconductors and their heterostructures, it highlights my independent research program: identifying physical problems, developing predictive theories, and initiating new directions with experimentalists. The first part addresses Kane fermions in bulk HgCdTe: temperature-driven band inversion, domain-wall states, the collapse of Landau levels in crossed electric and magnetic fields, and disorder-induced topological transitions. The second examines pressure-, temperature-, and disorder-driven phase transitions in single and double HgTe quantum wells (QWs), including bilayer-graphene-like semimetals and a two-dimensional higher-order topological insulator (2D HOTI) phase beyond the minimal BHZ model. The third develops three-layer InAs/Ga(In)Sb QWs as a III-V platform for massless Dirac fermions, large-gap quantum spin Hall insulators, 2D HOTI phases, and semimetals with quadratic band touching, and discusses InAs$_{x}$Sb$_{1-x}$/InAs$_{y}$Sb$_{1-y}$ heterostructures as a promising alternative. Several of these predictions are supported by experimental observations, including quantized helical edge transport up to 60 K and the unconventional quantum Hall effect. Defended on March 25, 2026, at the University of Montpellier. Jury

papers.title: Generation of Bloch Points with Controlled Spin Texture Using Geometrical Boundary Conditions
Cooperative Boundary Switching of Mesoscopic Real Spectra in a Non-Hermitian Chain Family
papers.abs: At fixed bulk criticality, every fixed nonsingular real single-end potential preserves a growing local population of real eigenvalues in an open analytic family of non-Hermitian chains. An open region of two-end real potentials removes this population. A boundary-amplitude criterion fixes the minimum number of controlled ends. The population grows as $\sqrt N$, where $N$ is chain length, although its normalized spectral weight vanishes and the local limiting bands remain unchanged. For a representative chain's four zero-detuning settings, an independent passive Hermitian double chain converts this distinction into separated resonances at one fixed local port under a common coupling scan at fixed probe carrier. Its absolute reflection contrast and stability margin both scale as $N^{-1}$, with explicit sufficient resource budgets. Boundary amplitudes thus fix a minimum control requirement that limiting bands and thermodynamic spectral density do not specify.

papers.title: Topological superconductivity in layered d-wave altermagnetic metals
papers.abs: We investigate multilayer d-wave altermagnetic metals with odd-parity helical p-wave pairing. In the minimal bilayer system, interlayer tunneling reconstructs the spin-split Fermi surfaces and generates two layer-hybridized sectors with distinct effective chemical potentials. Without Rashba spin-orbit coupling (RSOC), the emergent mirror symmetry and subsystem chiral symmetry stabilize phases with different numbers of helical Majorana edge-mode pairs and additional counterpropagating pairs, jointly characterized by the mirror Chern number and the winding numbers defined along high-symmetry lines. The combination of RSOC and the altermagnetic exchange field gaps out the helical Majorana pairs while, in a certain parameter regime, leaving another pair of counterpropagating Majorana edge modes gapless, giving rise to second-order topological phases with isolated or twofold Majorana corner modes, as well as a hybrid-order phase in which gapless Majorana edge modes coexist with Majorana corner modes. We identify a layer symmetry that elucidates the physical origin of these phases. For an arbitrary N-layer system, such a symmetry naturally arises from the interlayer-coupling matrix, allowing N-fold Majorana corner modes to emerge when all layer-hybridized sectors enter the nontrivial second-order regime. Our results establish the interplay among the layer degree of freedom, odd-parity pairing, and Fermi-surface configurations as a controllable route to engineering topological superconductivity in layered altermagnetic systems.

papers.title: Non-Abelian quantum Hall states at strong Landau level mixing: finding anyons with first-principles AI
papers.abs: Non-Abelian anyons, strange particles forming the basis of fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, are predicted to emerge in fractional quantum Hall states at even-denominator filling factors. Identifying which topological order is realized has proven to be a challenging problem that requires an accurate, non-perturbative treatment of realistic Landau level mixing, which has so far been missing from theoretical studies. Here we present the first complete solution of non-Abelian quantum Hall problem that includes all electrons and all Landau levels, for spin-polarized electrons at filling factor $ν= 3/2$. We develop a momentum-resolved neural-network variational wave function, optimized solely on the microscopic Hamiltonian, which gives direct access to the topologically degenerate ground states. Without any physics input about the expected outcome, it discovers a degenerate ground-state manifold whose entanglement reveals anyons with quantum dimension $\sqrt{2}$, the hallmark of Ising-type non-Abelian order. By directly computing the overlap with trial wave functions, we further show that Landau level mixing favors the anti-Pfaffian over other candidate states. Our results demonstrate the power of neural-network wave functions in finding and characterizing non-Abelian anyons from first principles, in regimes of strong Landau level mixing, relevant to many recent experiments.

papers.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
papers.abs: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. At v = 1/3 and 2/3, we observe backscattering resonances with three times the frequency, consistent with resonant transmission of e/3 charges via a single anyon transistor. We demonstrate controlled depletion to the last quasiparticle to form a single anyon quantum dot. Tracing the charge addition spectrum for quasiparticle number Nqp = 1-5, we observe highly irregular addition energies, consistent with DMRG modeling showing a complex orbital shell-filling behavior. At higher Nqp = 10-20, the addition energies show a striking pattern: quasiholes at 1/3 (and quasiparticles at 2/3) show a regular addition spectrum while quasiparticles at 1/3 (and quasiholes at 2/3) do not. papers.title: Engineering Color and Angular Stability in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics Using Metal-Oxide Photonic Glasses
papers.abs: Coloring building-integrated photovoltaics poses a dilemma: absorptive pigments cost photocurrent, while ordered photonic structures are iridescent. Amorphous photonic glasses, disordered packings of high-index nanospheres, are proposed to avoid both, yet their angle-independent color has rarely been quantified on a realistic module stack. A non-absorbing scatterer needs a high index with visible transparency, which the Moss rule caps near 2.35. Coupling Mie scattering, the Percus-Yevick structure factor, the exact phase function, and two-flux transfer with absorption and refraction at the front glass, we fix four target colors that a crowd-sourced naming survey calls unambiguously blue, green, gold, and terracotta, and map the recipes reaching them across four metal oxides, four encapsulants, two cell technologies, and wide ranges of particle size, packing fraction, and layer number. All four are reached in a laminated three-layer coating, to within DeltaE00 of 0.8 to 2.5, but not from one oxide: transparent TiO2 renders the blue and only pale warm tones; the green, gold, and terracotta require the blue-band absorption of V2O5, and the low-contrast oxides turn grey at the warm end. The encapsulant governs the color, and the cell technology does not. Disorder does not confer angle independence: the colors hold for an observer moving under a fixed sun but drift by DeltaE00 of 5 to 18 over the day, terracotta least, and a facade lit from above and viewed from below shifts every color towards the blue.
